summary_paragraph: A male patient was admitted with a chief complaint of burning epigastric pain radiating to the mouth, associated with a bitter taste and mild shortness of breath. Given his history of peptic ulcer disease, GERD, and cardiac risk factors, he was admitted to rule out myocardial infarction. Initial evaluation showed no ischemic changes on EKG, normal cardiac enzymes, and symptom improvement with omeprazole and a GI cocktail. The pain was determined to be due to gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD). He remained hemodynamically stable, with resolution of symptoms during the stay. Chronic conditions including hypertension, aortic stenosis, chronic hyponatremia, and bronchitis were monitored and managed without intervention. He was discharged home with service, on optimized GERD therapy including omeprazole, with plans for H. pylori breath testing and follow-up with his gastroenterologist.
